title: Which Days of Grace Govern the Span an Arrears Figure is Struck Over
content:
The span over which an arrears figure on one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders is struck is governed by days of grace, and which days of grace govern is settled against the member's Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment.

## The rule

1. Where the medical plan enrollment the rider hangs on allows more days of grace than the rider held, the days of grace that enrollment allows govern the span.
2. Where the rider stands ended, no days of grace govern it at all.
3. Otherwise, the days of grace the rider held allows govern the span.

This bears on the span alone and not on whether the days of grace have run out.

## The days of grace each rider allows

| Rider | Days of grace allowed |
|---|---|
| Ridgecrest Preventive Dental Rider | 60 |
| Ridgecrest Vision Plus Rider | 60 |
| Ridgecrest Hearing Advantage Rider | 60 |
| Ridgecrest Comprehensive Dental Rider | 60 |
| Ridgecrest Premier Dental Rider | 90 |
| Ridgecrest Dental Vision Hearing Bundle Rider | 90 |

The days of grace the Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment allows are a term of that enrollment, read from the member's medical plan records.

## What the governing days of grace then do

The days of grace that govern are reckoned into whole months at thirty days to the month, any part month being dropped, and the span runs back over that many whole calendar months from the handling date. Where no days of grace govern, the span is empty and no entry falls inside it.

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

- A rider allowing 60 days of grace, on a medical plan enrollment allowing 90: the enrollment allows more, so 90 days govern, giving a span of 3 whole months.
- A rider allowing 90 days of grace, on a medical plan enrollment allowing 30: the enrollment does not allow more, so the rider's 90 days govern, giving a span of 3 whole months.
- A rider allowing 60 days of grace, on a medical plan enrollment allowing 60: the enrollment does not allow more than the rider, so the rider's 60 days govern, giving a span of 2 whole months.
- A rider standing ended: no days of grace govern, the span is empty, and no entry falls inside it.
